column1: # The patch log: what changed in the engine and when, one line each.
# Typed by hand like a changelog is; read by scripts/webapp.py for the
# Patches page. Newest first. Columns: date, area, note.

column3: The bettor's operating decision for the long run: play what the board allows — PLAY cards at or above their bar, watch lanes only when a book of his own clears the bar — and stop hunting own reads. His own reads had graded 83.9% at +7.2% on 31 archived bets, but finding them meant verifying a choice already made against the engine's searches, which felt like gambling. The record from here is the rule's record

Session #6 opens on the 2 Sep board as PRE-ALFA 2, the long run: the engine and its rules are not touched while it runs. Sessions #4-5 archived whole in archive/2026-08-28-sessions-4-5-odds-layer/ — Tip 1 80.9% on 267, playable 78.0%, bets 113/143 at ROI −0.3%

Early or closing, measured on the same 8,506 cards: the market drifts away from Athena's side toward kickoff (early price lower 61% of the time), but the bar applied at the early price plays fewer cards for more — cards that clear only because the price drifted out late return −3.67% in both seasons. Rule: decide at first sight, buy later if it has drifted out

Blended probability tested as the guard and declined: every card-tracking bar negative at real prices, the five coarse labels +0.93% in both seasons. The label works as a bar because the market cannot see through it card by card

Bankroll replay: €50 at 4% of the running balance, day-granular, every betting day a start. All plays at best-of-market €63.70 with a 49.5% drawdown; at one book €35; the strong lane alone €106 and every year-long start above €50
Age-aware cross-division fallback A/B (count 82.10 / age 82.06 / union 81.71 on 2,683 eligible fixtures) — declined; the count gate stays, behind a mode switch for the next idea

BUG: the fuzzy matcher scored a reserve side as a perfect match for its parent club (Jong Ajax read AFC Ajax; Ceuta v Celta Fortuna was priced off Celta Vigo's La Liga form). names.reserve_side draws the line; the fuzzy pass never crosses it

sweep.py --set "Home v Away" 2-1 grades one kicked-off fixture by hand through the same settle() as the feed, for the leagues no feed carries (Swiss, Polish, Algerian). The Gladbach card was invisible to the ESPN matcher; two nickname rows

Seven seasons the store never had: openfootball abandoned FRA-L2, ESP-L2, GER-B2, TUR-SL 2025-26 in November and never published SUI-SL 2025-26, SWE-AL and NOR-EL 2025. 1,921 results filled from football-data, 40 cards re-priced, guard slices rebuilt. Five board names that resolved to nothing aliased (OH Leuven, LAFC, Atlético-MG, Junior Barranquilla, Chongqing)
Reprice honours a WITHDRAWAL: a card the engine abstains on at reprice says so in its cell instead of keeping the old tip. The ledger keeps a bet whose card has no tip

BUG: five guards drifted — the test suite red since 28 Aug (unknown push mark), the forward log stamping every renamed lane as a new sighting (24 fixtures counted twice), the ledger CLI with its own settlement rules, started() pinned to UTC+2, two non-atomic writes. All closed; suite 126 green

The struck lane is exactly two rungs: U3.0 bought as U3.5 and U4.25 as U4.5, and only while the engine's own winning_totals says they are the same bet. The over-side rule that turned O1.5 into O1.0 (a different bet, quoted at 1.01) was wrong and is gone
A match that has kicked off is not playable: quotes stop at kickoff and the verdict checks the clock, after three of four plays turned out to be matches in progress

One club, one name, store-wide: canonical spellings folded with a day test (a club plays at most once a day), primary by latest-played. 552 folds, hidden rows 22% → 0.8%, 179 abstentions recovered, tip 1 unchanged

The confluence guard ships: five labels from the card's tier and an as-of score built from the board's own searches, frozen thresholds validated on two windows over 62,528 replayed picks. The decline rule on top: PLAY only when the best quote clears the label's break-even by 6%, never on red. STRONG marks a top-quartile score in Europe
Live bookmaker prices: the odds layer's first working piece. The card shows what the market pays, best book named, and stamps what it said at first sight into the forward log

BUG: Ask Athena's filter matched nothing on lane words — 'team over' and 'tip 2' both returned 0 of 713. Cause was an escaping trap: the page is built from one big Python f-string, and a JS regex written as \\b there is parsed by PYTHON first, where \\b is the backspace character. The rendered regex therefore demanded an invisible control character before the O or U and never matched, so no over/under, team or tip-2 tokens ever entered a bank card's haystack — while the result-lane tokens, whose regex has no escapes, worked fine and hid the breakage. Both regexes now use (?:^|[^A-Za-z]) instead of a word boundary, which needs no backslash at all. Verified in node against the real Premier League bank: 'team over' 271 rows, 'tip 1 under' 387 at 87.1%, 'draw no bet' 230 at 82.2% on tip 3

BUG: this session's fixtures were counted TWICE in the bank. Merging the board's own results into the results store (31 Aug) meant the matchbank rebuild replayed them as retro rows, while webapp still appended the live board copy — 288 duplicated fixtures. The hero window, which takes the 300 most recent graded playable lanes, was therefore built from a doubled weekend and read 78.0% instead of 80.7%. The board rows are now dropped where a retro row already covers the fixture (the retro row wins: it carries all three graded lanes), and the hero computation moved after that pass, since it had been running before it. The bettor spotted the drop and asked whether the retrosim caused it — it did, through the ingest, but the honest number was never as low as the page said

A league on its own is now a valid Ask Athena query: it returns everything the bank holds for that competition, newest first — 821 rows for the Championship, 713 for the Premier League — and the filter bar below cuts it down, which is the point (the bettor: search a league, then filter team over). A date still narrows within a league as before. Bank cards became compact and expandable: the summary carries the score, the date and a chip per graded lane, and 'more' opens the three cells in full, so a several-hundred-row answer reads as a scoreboard rather than a wall. Head-to-head answers and short lists open by default

The match bank now carries and grades ALL THREE lanes on every one of its 30,275 fixtures — the bettor asked for it so the bank could be cross-examined the way the board can. matchbank.py runs each fixture through the same two_tips path a live card uses and stores tip 1, tip 2 and tip 3 with their own marks, formatted by the board's own cell1/cell2/cell3 so the text is identical. Coverage: tip 1 on 30,220, tip 2 on 22,503 (74%), tip 3 on 12,722 (42%) — the lower two only print above their own bars, which is the honest number, not a gap. Ask Athena's results gain the fourth counter and the result-lane vocabulary. Bank-wide the three read 83.8 / 69.7 / 78.9, within a point of the 300-window baselines computed independently

Ask Athena's results get the same filter and a counter. A bank card now carries the board's search vocabulary — teams, competition, country, date, lane kind, and its own mark — so a league-and-date lookup can be narrowed further and scored: 'tip 1 under' inside the Premier League bank returns 389 matches at 87.1%, 'tip 1 over' 321 at 79.4%. Two counters rather than four, because the bank grades ONE lane: retrosim rows carry tip 1's mark and nothing else, tip 2 only where a board row supplied it, and tip 3 is not in the bank at all (it postdates the retrosim). The counter says 'tip 1 · bank' so it cannot be mistaken for the board's four

Found bets joins the filter: a bet row now carries its fixture's league, code and country plus its own lane kind (team over, double chance, draw no bet, match under) and its mark, so 'netherlands' returns the Eredivisie and Eerste Divisie positions together and 'team over' returns every team over taken. The counter row becomes tab-aware — four lane records on Completed, ONE taken-bets record on Found bets, nothing on the two pending tabs where there is nothing to score. Unfiltered the bets counter reproduces the tile exactly (104/130). First readings worth keeping: double chances 88.0% on 25, draw-no-bets 64.3% on 14

The filter learns countries, folds accents, and reserves exact matching for collisions a country word cannot break. config/countries.tsv maps a league code's prefix to its country (typed like the nickname file — culture, not data, and the engine never reads it), so 'spain', 'brazil', 'japan' work. Every haystack also carries an accent-free copy and the query is folded, so 'serie b' finds 'Série B' and 'brasileirao' finds 'Brasileirão'. Exact matching now fires only where the colliding names share a country — laliga inside laliga 2, bundesliga inside 2. bundesliga, brasileirao inside brasileirao serie b — because there no country term can separate them. Italy's Serie B inside Brazil's stays a substring, so 'brazil, serie b' (12) and 'italy, serie b' (10) both resolve, exactly as the bettor asked

The filter learns lane KINDS and gains comma-AND. A card's haystack now carries what each lane is, not just the fixture's names: team over, team under, match over, match under, double chance, draw no bet, result lane, playable, capped, and the settled mark (hit/miss/push). Commas narrow rather than widen — 'real madrid, team over' is the Madrid card that also offers a team over — and the live counters recount over whatever survives. Board-wide the vocabulary resolves: 109 team overs, 26 team unders, 76 draw-no-bets, 60 double chances

The filter bar becomes an analysis tool: four counters under the search box recount final pick / tip 1 / tip 2 / tip 3 over whatever the filter leaves on screen — a league, a club, a rung, anything the haystack matches — and show the whole run when the box is empty. Every settled card carries its own four grades as data attributes (tip 1 and tip 2 at the playable standard, tip 3 whole, the star's own lane for the final pick), so the page counts marks rather than re-deriving anything from text. Verified against the tiles: unfiltered, the counters read 80.3 / 79.5 / 67.4 / 78.2 — the same four numbers

The Prob column goes universal: scripts/lane_price.py prices ANY lane on a boarded fixture, not just the ones the card printed. The bettor asked for a number on their own reads — the one part of the book that had none, and the part where a number is most useful. Three engine figures per fixture (goal expectation, each side's chance to score) are enough to price the whole lane space: ladder rungs through p_win, team rungs through the same curves on one side's gf, result lanes through the tilted Poisson pair behind Tip 3. Computed once per fixture and cached in config/lane_cache.json (derived — delete it and the next render rebuilds it), so the table gains a probability for every row without a per-bet engine call. Verified against the cards: a lane the card DID print reprices to the same number. Dashes now mean only one thing — the engine abstains on that fixture. 144 bets, 0 dashes

BUG: the cross-division fallback for promoted clubs has been dead. Scaling an adjacent division's goals writes fractional values into fixtures.tsv's int64 goal columns, and pandas raises rather than upcasting — so every club whose history lives one division down crashed the whole request and the card printed an abstention. Found when Lincoln v Blackburn failed to price (Athletico Paranaense had failed the same way earlier and was worked around by renaming, which was the wrong diagnosis). Goals are cast to float before scaling; Lincoln and Athletico both price now. The fallback was shipped and validated back in the era when pandas upcast silently — a reminder that a dependency can retire a feature without anyone editing it

Rule 7 gains its second clause, from the day's worst pocket: SKIP tip 2 lanes and skip the Rule 6 HARDER-line translations. The Norwegian 17:00 wall took three tickets of exactly those shapes and lost all three (Kristiansund U1.5 team lane 1.41, IK Start U3.5 harder 1.41, Tromsø O2.5 harder 1.50), and Randers' team over — bought at 1.83, above its ask — was cashed out at 0.63x rather than lost whole. This is not one bad evening read as law: the final-picking replay already measured tip 2 lanes 12.7 points below tip 1 on 16,554 fixtures, and the star was restricted to tip 1 or tip 3 for the same reason this morning. The ledger now matches the card. Ledger also gains partial cash-outs: column 5 holds the return multiple rather than a flag, so 0.63 books what actually came back

The baseline bar leads with the FINAL PICK — the card's starred lane replayed over each league's last 300 matches (82.1%), in front of the per-tip baselines — and the first tile becomes the session's own final-pick record: the same chooser applied to every completed fixture of the run. config/final_pick.tsv is written by final_pick.py --write, so both numbers derive from the instrument rather than from anything typed. First reading: baseline 82.1%, session 81.8% on 159 graded — the replay and the live run agree to within three tenths of a point

scripts/ingest_board.py ships — the board's completed matches now merge into the results bank (157 results into 28 leagues on first run). Resolver-guarded: a name that does not match the store is printed and skipped, never guessed (10 skipped, PSG/LAFC-style abbreviations); store.save deduplicates so re-running after each sweep is idempotent. As-of replay discipline is untouched — windows simply reach the current week now

Every card now marks exactly ONE preferred lane — the ★ falls through the full protocol (weak/capped -> tip 3; playable tip 1; playable tip 2; any printed result lane; tip 1 as the engine's own pick). scripts/final_pick.py replays this exact chooser per league at n=300 against always-tip-1; verdict lands when the run finishes

BUY_REACH_CAP 0.03 ships — the bettor flagged tip 2 buy-from prices pulled absurdly low by the blend (−15% margin brackets on sub-60 team lanes). Measured before correcting: 8,404 team-lane offers land within two points of their claims in BOTH half-windows (sub-65: says 59.1 lands 59.2 / says 58.8 lands 57.0), so a 56% lane's fair price really is ~1.79 and the uncapped blend printing 1.47 reached 18% below reality. The blend now lifts the pricing probability at most 3 points above the lane's own number; its role above the record (asking extra of easy lanes) is untouched. 33 pending cards repriced

The protocol's accent, on the card itself: a gold-rimmed '★ read first' lane. Strong-tier leagues (tip 1 baseline 85%+ on the replay) accent a playable tip 1; weak-tier (under 80%) and consensus-capped leagues accent tip 3 — the bettor's observation that the tiers invert between the two tips, made visible. Tiers derive from baselines.tsv, so accents move when the replay is re-run; settled cards drop the accent since it is reading guidance, not a grade. 31 lanes accented on today's board (24 tip 1, 7 tip 3)

Protocol step 2 lands in the layout: in a league whose tip 1 baseline runs under 80% (derived from baselines.tsv) or a consensus-capped one, a card whose tip 1 did not clear the playable bar now leads with tip 3 — the bettor's observation that the top lane should be the one worth reading first, the same principle as the playable tab's lead swap. Settled cards keep tip 1 order for consistent grading. Two cards flip on today's slate: Andorra-Eibar (capped L2) and Rennes-Le Mans (weak-tier Ligue 1)

The About page gains 'How to read a card — the bettor's protocol': badge first (level AND delta), tip 3 in weak or capped leagues (measured: tip 3 is flat across league tiers, 80.8/79.9/78.4 against tip 1's 77.7/82.4/86.5 — it reads who is stronger, not how many goals, so it survives totals-chaos), DNB/1X over 12 at equal says, and the Rule 7 price gate last. The tier table derives from baselines.tsv at render, so it moves when the replay is re-run

Rule 7, measured on this session's settled book: NO ticket on a lane the engine never priced (the Prob dash — 8/11 landed but ROI −9.7%), NO result-lane ticket below its printed buy≥, and DNB never under ~1.35 — the DNB pocket graded 0W 4P 4L for −50% ROI because the draw shelters the stake while paying nothing, and every loser was either unpriced or bought below the asking price. The rule deliberately KEEPS the R6 softer unders bought a few cents under buy≥ (40 tickets, 87.5%, +8.3% ROI — push protection the claim never priced) and points result-lane money at the draw-covering shapes instead (12/X2 book: 7W 1L). One session, small pockets (5, 8, 11 tickets) — orange until a second window confirms
Stake unit raised 0.80 → 0.90 (4% of bank) from the overnight Americas onward — the ledger keeps scoring flat units, so hitrate and ROI are unaffected; only the money behind each unit grew

Tip 3 ships on probation — the result lane the engine always refused to touch, proposed by the bettor and measured before building (15,048 fixtures): strongest double chance from 0.72, DNB upgrade when one side holds 0.65 of the no-draw mass, home tilt 1.10 closing the one systematic gap. fixtures.tsv grows an 8th column (after status, so every old index survives), the sweep grades result lanes on the final score with the DNB draw as the family's one push, and the lane stays out of every tally until live results earn it in

The team-lane STREAK DEBIT ships — the bettor asked whether staff/squad churn data would fix side attribution; the results-only shadow of it (recent stub diverging from the long record) measured monotone with overclaim on 8,404 offers and both half-windows agree in the top band. Published probability and edge debited 0.05 per goal of aligned excess above 0.35; a debited lane must still clear MIN_EDGE or it stops printing. Depth-of-record and league-table variants measured dead and are declined

A pushed tip counts as a HIT in every tally — the bettor's rule: the standing offset plays the printed rung a notch softer (U3.0 → U3.5), and the actual play wins where the rung pushes. Applied to the header counters, playable tallies and the hero window; the ◦ glyph stays on the card for honesty. The root version (push into the published probabilities) is logged orange — it reshuffles selection and needs the full two-window treatment

Card badges retold: the league line now shows the PLAYABLE record and its distance from baseline — (83.7 +1.7) instead of the old all-tips hitrate — because the playable number is the one a bettor actually lives on; consensus-cap leagues show (82.0 capped) instead of pretending a subset they no longer have

The buy≥ price now listens to the league: computed on a blend of the tip and its league's playable record (0.4/0.6 below the record, 0.8/0.2 above — continuous at the join), the bettor's rule for making lower-probability lanes reachable at real-world odds while asking a little extra of easy ones. Every card prints the margin the price still holds over the tip's own break-even, negative included — the reach is visible, never hidden. BUY_BLEND_BELOW/ABOVE join the verified Engine state block

CONSENSUS_CAP_LEAGUES ships — the bettor's reading of the new Playable-hit column found seven leagues (CRO-1L, MEX-LMX, IRL-PD, MAR-BP, COL-PA, ESP-L2, ITA-SA) whose above-bar lanes run a flat 6–7 points hot in both half-windows while their consensus lanes underclaim. Published probability there is now capped at the market's league-baseline chance, so edge never exceeds zero and no lane badges playable; board playable hit 82.1 → 82.6. retrosim gains --dump (per-tip rows) so the bar itself was swept: no threshold beats +1%, the bar stands

Retrosim gains a 'Playable hit' column: the same replay narrowed to lanes above the +1% bar, with the subset's tip count — the bettor was right that the Hit column had no filter, and the two now sit side by side (NGA-PL 90.5 all / 88.7 playable; JPN-J1 88.6 / 90.0). All 58 rows re-run via retrosim --write, gaps now graded on the REL-debited published number (board-wide +0.8)

The three operating commands audited and their contracts written down. Finding: 'futurematch' never existed as a script — every slate and re-price was throwaway code retyping the card format from memory. scripts/futurematch.py now owns it (slate mode + --reprice), retrosim gains --write so the hitrates table refresh is part of the instrument, and the README states exactly what each command must write
Stage renamed: BETA STAGE 2 → PRE-ALFA 1, on the app header and the README title

REL_SAYS_DEBIT ships — the bettor asked whether a tip's distance from its league's own hitrate predicts misses. It does, one-sided: claims past league+2 run hot (wide band −5.6 in both windows), so the published number is pulled back at 1.1 per excess point. Cards re-priced: CHN-SL's raw 90s now print ~83, two lanes fall honestly below the playable bar

The last stragglers settled into their era: Barcelona ✅ 2-0, Partizan ✅ 2-1, Hibernian ❌ 2-3 — Session #3 closes finally at Tip 1 81.9% on 72, playable 84.3%, bets ROI −7.5%. The two Algerian rows are recorded as ungraded forever (no source). The live board is now purely Session #4: 41 Friday fixtures, 18 positions
Session #4 opens with 18 positions logged (the widened strategy) and the ledger learns double chance: X2/1X settle as win-unless-the-other-side-wins, alignment chip 'own read · DC'

Session #3 archived whole (archive/2026-08-24-session-3-cup-run): Tip 1 82.4% on 68, playable 85.1%, bets ROI −8.6%. Session #4 opens on Friday's 41 fixtures plus six closing-night stragglers (Larne's open U3.5 among them); README rebuilt fresh with the era's record pointing at the archive

The reads claimed 'the table' but compute it from results alone — and CSL 2026 docks points, so Shenhua read 4th while sitting 9th official. Results verified correct against ESPN match by match; only the wording lied. Reads now say 'by results this season' / 'chasing the top', which is both true and the more relevant number for goals; 'promotion/europe hunt' retired (it read as nonsense in China and Saudi Arabia)

Playable cards lead with the lane that made them playable — a fixture on the tab through its Tip 2 no longer headlines a sub-bar Tip 1 (Llaneros showed U4.25 −1.5% while its O1.75 +2.3% hid behind 'more')

Grading defect found by the bettor, not the verifier: ESPN's keyEvents feed silently drops goal events, and counting an incomplete list graded Plzeň 2-1 when the 90 ended 4-1. regulation() now reads the RUNNING SCORE from the goal narration (commentary feed first) — every ET row re-verified: Plzeň ✅→❌ 4-1, Raków ✅→❌ 2-2, Celje's score text corrected, eight others confirmed. Hitrate 85.5 → 81.8, ROI −1.6 → −6.7 — the honest numbers

Hardcoded: a match in extra time settles immediately — the 90 is history the moment ET kicks off, so the sweep grades it from the goal timeline (ESPN STATUS_OVERTIME / period 3+) instead of holding a decided bet open. First live test: Jablonec 1-0 and Qarabağ 1-2 both settled mid-ET, both U4.25 hits

Found bets gains an 'Athena says' column — each position's relation to the published tip, derived from the board: = Tip 1/2, a Rule-6 softer/harder neighbour, the Rule-5 DNB lane, a team lane on its own read, or off board. The run's shape at a glance: 21 of 35 are Rule-6 ladder plays, 7 DNB, 3 exact tips, 2 off board

Proof in hindsight: the pre-calibration era (69.9% on 73 undisciplined bets, ROI −10.1) replayed through today's engine grades 84.2% take-all and 83.3% at the playable bar; the first calibrated slate's 63 lanes filter to 42 at the bar and hit 95.0%. The gap between the old record and today's number is discipline plus calibration, measured — with the in-sample caveat stated: these are the very weeks the constants were tuned on

Both archived eras replayed on the finished engine with the bet counterfactual (changed lane + bet = unplaced; changed lane + no bet = placed on the new lane): first slate 14/63 lanes change, bets 80.8 → 83.3; pre-calibration 36/118, bets 69.9 → 71.2 — the record survives its own counterfactual, in-sample caveat noted

Calibration day summarised in the README and About: the Retrosim page forced every number to be defended, and one page built to display numbers ended up correcting the engine — board-wide retrosim hit 82.4 → 83.7 on the same fixtures

Pending rows re-priced on the finished engine: MC Alger carries the high-says debit (93.3 → 92.1), Celta v Osasuna genuinely re-priced on fresh results (O1.5 → U4.25, out of playable), no pending tip moved by the floors — tonight's slate has none of the fourteen floored leagues

The search bank widened to the test-run window — 60 competitions, ~30k graded matches on the current build (was ~11.5k on stale floors) — Ask Athena answers far more matchups and the hero window grows to the 500 most recent graded playable lanes

Balance audited as hit × buy≥: the corners are honest (long odds pay for low hit and vice versa) — the real imbalance is the five overconfident leagues (MLS, ESP-L2, MEX-LMX, UEL-Q, FRA-L2) whose printed price their hit cannot cover; flagged for calibration or cull

The floors re-decided under an ROI constraint the first pass missed: hitrate must not be bought with unbuyable rungs. Highest floor keeping ≥2/3 of playable volume — six leagues at 0.82, one at 0.80, seven at 0.78, and GRE-SL and PER-L1 REVERTED (GRE-SL's 91.7 came at 66% → 6% playable share, a mirage). Retrosim gains a buy-from column so this can never hide again

The cup playbook transplanted: probability floor 0.82 on the sixteen weakest domestic leagues — selection climbs to safer rungs, both windows improve in every one (ENG-L2 80.6→88.9, ITA-SA 79.1→88.5, GRE-SL 80.9→91.7), zero volume cost. MLS declined (the floor makes it worse) and ITA-SB has no soft rungs to climb to

Back-to-top fixed: an inline handler runs with the element in scope and Element has its own scrollTo, so the bare call scrolled the button's own content and silently did nothing — window.scrollTo now, verified 2552 → 0
websitebanner_4 heads the Retrosim page, same treatment as the others

Banners: hero on Home with the title and a live subheader — Tip 1 over the 300 most recent graded playable lanes, computed from the match bank at render so it can never rot — and page banners on About and Past sessions

The full table re-measured: 58 leagues, 29,763 fixtures, weighted gap −0.3 with the debits in. Two rows survive at real sample size — TUR-SL −5.2 and ESP-L2 −4.3, both concentrated in their most recent two seasons — and only those two now color red

HIGH_SAYS_DEBIT 0.012: above says 90% the domestic board reads a measured 1.2 points hot (32,493 tips, 45 leagues, both windows, stronger in the played set) — published probability, edge and buy≥ carry the debit, selection stays raw

The retrosim table re-measured at up to 800 fixtures per league (two-season cap): the worst rows were noise at n=200 — ROU-L1 −11.6 is really −2.8 — and the whole table now grades the published number, debits included
IRL-PD's mu is anti-correlated with outcomes (slope −2.8, t −3.0, both windows) and MAR-BP reads the same way weaker — flagged as cull candidates; their hitrates survive on the league mean alone

Every lane tab sorts: probability, edge, league hitrate — highest first — plus overs-first and unders-first, which group by side and rank by probability inside the group. Cards carry their own keys, so no sort re-reads rendered text
Retrosim hitrates sort on any column, click again to reverse; a number opens on its largest, a name opens at A

The ledger of everything tried: 20 verified, 6 unfinished, 22 declined, typed once in config/hypotheses.tsv and rendered into both the README and the app — a rejected idea keeps the number that rejected it so it is not re-proposed

Retrosim badges were a day stale on all six cup codes — written before the signed gap shipped. Re-run: UCL 84.0 (+0.5), UEL 88.5 (+3.9), UECL 86.0 (+0.3), UCL-Q 82.5, UEL-Q 84.0, UECL-Q 84.8; the two big gaps closed from +4.4 and +4.2 to near zero
The Engine state block is now checked against the live code on every render — it had sat dated 24 Aug while DEFENSE_BLEND, the whole Club Elo lane and the 0.82 cup floor shipped underneath it
About gains a run-sessions section: what a run is, why the next run is the only honest test, and the arc from 84.2% at ROI −10.1% to a calibrated board

The +1% bar checked against this run's own settled rows: Tip 1 grades 75.0 held (says 82.7, gap -7.7), 86.7 at +1-3%, 100 at +3%+ — the withheld band is the only one that grades BELOW its stated probability. Confirms where the bar sits; 12 rows do not move it

The sweep was blind to three continents: ESPN files a fixture under the COMPETITION's local day, so a Chilean 18:00 sat on our previous date and was reported missing — neighbouring days are asked for too and merged

Club identity across sources hardened: ø/đ/ł/æ/ß folded (Lillestrøm was not Lillestrom) and translated names resolved through the nickname file (Red Star Belgrade is Crvena zvezda) — no fuzzy rule could ever have paired those
Live lanes state what the score has done to them — landed, needs N more, room for N, half gone — read from the ledger's own settlement, on every tab and in the README

One update is never one match: scripts/sweep.py checks every unsettled fixture against ESPN, grades finished ones on the 90 (extra time peeled off the scoreline) and refuses to leave neighbours stale; the renderer fails on any fixture four hours past kickoff with no result

The renderer now verifies itself: every fixture must appear on every surface it belongs to, tallies must match, the ledger must be complete and the app script must parse — a mismatch refuses to finish
